title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'entered the world' joins hereditary vice, not bare actual
pass_a_gloss: That suggests further arguments, which for brevity I put elsewhere. Add that I have already proved actual did not enter the world—that is, into humans: so the attribute 'entered into the world' joins itself to sin not as it means bare actual, but as it means the vice sprung from it (immediately on my view; by God's imputation on yours). So I think my argument stands firm enough.
pass_b_english: Which suggests other arguments to me, but, for the sake of avoiding too much prolixity in this place, to be conferred to another place. Add that I have already proved that actual sin did not enter into the world, that is, into humans: whence it follows that this attribute entered into the world joins sin to itself, not insofar as it signifies actual sin, but insofar as it signifies the vice arisen from it in my opinion immediately, but in yours by the mediation of God's imputation. So I think I have confirmed my argument enough.
source_text: Id quod mihi alia suggerit argumenta, sed, vitandae hoc loco nimiae prolixitatis causa, conferenda in alium locum. Adde quod iam probavi peccatum actuale non introiisse in mundum, hoc est, in homines: unde sequitur hoc attributum in mundum introiit sibi iungere peccatum, non qua significat peccatum actuale, sed qua significat vitium ex eo mea sententia immediate, tua vero mediante Dei imputatione ortum. Sic opinor meum argumentum firmavi satis.
